text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: The paper presents a national-scale spatial land system change model (CLUMondo) for Cambodia, explicitly simulating future land use/land cover (LULC) changes to 2040 under three distinct policy scenarios. Its primary objective is to evaluate how large-scale land acquisition (LSLA) governance affects future LULC patterns—specifically tree cover, natural areas, and land system composition—with mapped projections as core outputs. It implements ≥2 future scenarios (Hands-off, Penalization, Proactive Granting) with quantitative comparisons of LULC outcomes (e.g., area in Mha, conversion rates, core natural area metrics). The modeling is spatially explicit at 1 km resolution, includes quantitative metrics (e.g., 32% LSLA conversion in 2015, projected tree cover loss/gain, patch sizes), and produces mapped LULC projections. While tiger reintroduction is a conservation application, the central research question and modeling effort focus on predicting LULC changes under alternative policies, satisfying all core inclusion criteria and avoiding all exclusion criteria.)
